 Woman gets dumped, then goes viral after stumbling across a surprising group of supporters, ‘the most iconic way to go through a breakup’
 She's gotta be feeling better after that.
 By 
 Misty Layne 
 Nov 10th, 2026, 3:00 pm 
 Save us as a preferred source in Google 
 Share 
 Share 
 Share 
 Getting dumped is never fun, but after it happened to TikToker Grace Hackett  (@gracehacket) on November 9, 2026, she found her spirits lifted after coming across a surprising group of supporters — the cast of Chicago Fire . In a TikTok now gone viral with over 865,000 views, Hackett holds a bottle of wine while standing by the front stoop of a building where numerous cast members of the show, including Christian Stolte and Taylor Kinney, are hanging out while they playfully call out her now-ex-boyfriend.
 The text on the video read, “POV. Walking back home after you got dumped. Time to go watch Chicago Fire .” Hackett then captioned it, “Love a supportive cast! And walking through a TV set post breakup.” She later joked in the comments that she was now Chicago Fire ’s “biggest fan” after the encounter.
 The ‘Chicago Fire’ cast were happy to share their opinions on Hackett’s ex 
 It’s unclear what prompted the Chicago Fire cast to share their thoughts on Hackett’s ex, since the video begins with them doing just that, and Hackett provided little context. Stolte, who stars on the series as Randall “Mouch” McHolland, leaped up and exclaimed, “Hey, boy, did you screw up, Joe? You’ve made a huge mistake. What were you thinking, Joe?” The rest of the cast can be heard in the background, calling out things like, “Dumbest move of your life, Joe.”
 Stolte then informed the camera (and Joe), “Wait, wait, wait, we’re going to spend the rest of the night fighting over who gets to take this lady home and drink some wine with her, ok?” Hackett could be seen then, seemingly barely holding in her laughter. Stolte finished his tirade with: “You f***** up, Joe. Sorry.” At that point, the rest of the cast began to call Joe a jerk.
 Reactions to the video were amusing. One person wrote, “GIRL YOU HAVE MOUCH AND KELLY SEVERIDE HYPING YOU UP, YOU’RE LIVING MY DREAAAAAAM.” Another TikTok user pointed out the silver lining of Hackett’s breakup when they said, “I am so sorry about your breakup, babe, but this might be the most iconic way to go through a breakup.”
 While the video doesn’t explain the end of Hackett’s relationship, it seems like she’s having an easier time than some, like the guy whose partner of 3.5 years ghosted him one day . Plus, her breakup video is nearly as entertaining as the woman whose coffee shop breakup turned into a sitcom .
 ‘Chicago Fire’ just had its season 15 debut 
 Hackett’s video came not long after Chicago Fire ’s season 15 debut. The long-running series premiered its latest season on October 7, 2026. The show is going through some changes this year, as Dermot Mulroney, who played Battalion Chief Dom Pascal, made his final appearance in the season premiere. Joe Mińoso, who has played Firefighter Josef “Joe” Cruz since the first season and became a main character in season 2, also left the show this year with a final appearance in episode 5 titled “Three Hundred.”
 Fans (and those who don’t watch the show but want to learn more about the supportive guys in Hackett’s TikTok) can catch Chicago Fire Wednesdays at 9 p.m. ET/PT on NBC or Peacock. With a cast willing to support a heartbroken girl like that, the show is worth checking out.
